reader.title: Killing of Jessie Jones
bases: A town marshal is reported to have shot and killed the victim during an arrest, with no crowd or mob mentioned (A1).
The only report found is a one-sentence item in one Mississippi paper (A1); no other white or Black paper carrying it was found.

summary.text: The killing of Jessie Jones was the fatal shooting of a Black man named Jessie Jones by T. B. Murray, the marshal of a town printed as "Dlo," apparently in Mississippi, in or shortly before August 1905.
The only account found, a single sentence in The Leader of Brookhaven, Mississippi, said Jones was killed "while resisting arrest."
According to The Leader, Marshal Murray "shot and killed a negro named Jessie Jones while resisting arrest."
The item gave no date for the shooting, no reason for the attempted arrest and no description of how Jones was said to have resisted.
It also named no county or state, and the town appears only as "Dlo."
Because the sentence ran directly after the paper's "State Happenings" column of short Mississippi items, the shooting most likely took place in that state.
No report of an inquest, a charge against the marshal or any other official action appears in the coverage.
The Leader printed the news on page 6 of its 12 August 1905 issue, without a headline, as a short notice set beside other brief state news.
The item carried no attribution and presented the marshal's justification, that Jones was resisting arrest, as plain fact rather than as the officer's claim.
Jones was identified chiefly by race, as "a negro," while the marshal was named with his initials and office.
No other white newspaper reporting the shooting was found, and the Black press does not appear to have covered it.
